DodoRouter.Logs.CacheRegression.classify/1 — pure, I/O-free, in KeyHealth.classify style. Takes a session's ordered logs, returns :healthy | :insufficient_data | {:regressed, finding} where finding names diverged_at, through, pinned_read, turns and uncached_growth.

Keyed on read-vs-input rather than the epic's stated cache_write growth: cache_write_tokens is NULL on 733/740 dev rows, so a write test would be blind (noted on the epic). Cuts the session into comparable runs first — same provider+model (caches are model-scoped) and gaps within the 1h TTL — then looks for a streak of >=3 consecutive turns that fail to read back more than the turn before, over >2048 tokens of new input. A read stuck at 0 counts only if the run cached earlier, so sessions with no caching at all stay silent.

Accepting a verdict is now one click with an audit trail. Evaluations.apply_verdict/3 finds the routing step by the incumbent (the step whose {provider_key, model} matches what actually served the source request — zero or multiple matches refuse rather than guessing), updates only the identity fields (provider/key/model/plan_type derived from the key; temperature, max_tokens, reasoning_effort stay — the benchmark didn't measure changing them), and records a RoutingChangeEvent (new table, hot-upgrade safe, plain ids so the audit row outlives deleted steps/evals/keys, before/after snapshots carry key labels). revert_verdict restores the recorded before-state exactly once. Prompt-variant rows refuse — the system prompt lives in the client's code, not routing. UI: 'Route here' on ranking rows + applied-changes panel with revert on the eval page. MCP get_eval reads the trail as applied_changes (read-only by design — no routing-write scope exists for agents); guide + dashboard docs updated. 1430 green.

A shipped downgrade now keeps producing scores. EvalMonitor (one per evaluation, opt-in via 'Keep honest' on an applied change) anchors its baseline to the applied model's own benchmark ranking. MonitorSweeper (supervised GenServer, code_change/3 for hot upgrades, off under SQL sandbox) sweeps due monitors on its own timer; each sweep is judge-only — it scores the answers production actually served (served_answer reads both OpenAI and Anthropic wire shapes), bounded at sample_size per interval, and skips without spending when the judge key is unusable. Drift: rolling window of 6 scores, min 3, tolerance max(baseline stddev, 5); two consecutive dropped sweeps set alerted_at, recovery clears it — an anomaly describes the present. Monitor runs carry kind='monitor' and are excluded from every benchmark aggregate (latest_batch_runs, run counts, batch UI). UI panel with baseline/live-average/alert + pause/resume; MCP get_eval carries monitor read-only; guide + dashboard docs updated. 1435 green.

Per-decision replay shipped as comparison_mode: 'next_action' on evaluations. Each source log's request is the full frozen history (every real tool result — it happened, so no stub decay); the candidate proposes ONE next action via the existing replay primitive, and a specialized judge prompt shows RECORDED_ACTION vs CANDIDATE_ACTION and must state better/equivalent/worse alongside the usual 0-100 score — a missing preference fails the judge stage (cheap re-judge) rather than being coerced to a tie. Preferences are recorded only when asked for (rubric runs stay nil even though TestProvider now offers one), runs stamp judge_prompt_version v4-next-action so scores never masquerade as comparable, and monitors force rubric mode (the recorded action IS the live answer there). rankings gain a decisions rollup (better/equivalent/worse + preferred_pct); UI adds the judge-framing select and a 'Vs production' column; MCP create_eval takes comparison_mode, refuses actionless logs by name, from_eval_id clones the mode, get_eval carries decisions; guide + dashboard docs updated. 1442 green.

Variants can now patch any message, not just the system prompt. prompt_variants entries take message_patches: [{index, content}] — 0-based into the request as served, applied before any system_prompt prepend so indexes never shift; the caller computes the transform offline (the router never executes client code) and the first consumer is tool-result compression (rtk). An index with no message behind it is an error, not a skip — at replay time (:invalid_message_patch) and, over MCP, refused at creation with the (variant, log) pair named via a dry-run of every combination. The judge reads the patched request on both the sync and the re-judge path (Replays.patch_messages, the judge-side twin of patch_system_prompt). Changeset validates patch shape incl. distinct indexes; MCP schema + guide + agent-access docs updated. Seam-tested end to end: the candidate log and the judge log both carry the patched bytes while the as-served variant keeps the originals. 1448 green.

The epic's acceptance criteria is met end to end: an operator goes from recorded production traffic ('Benchmark this recording', evenly sampled, incumbents preseeded) to an evidence-backed verdict (per-source-log rankings, projected $/month at the capture's real traffic rate, per-decision next_action preference for agent trajectories, message-patch variants for context transforms) to an applied routing change ('Route here', audited via RoutingChangeEvent, revertible) — and the eval keeps running against live traffic afterward (EvalMonitor + MonitorSweeper judge served answers on a schedule, sustained drop below the benchmark baseline raises an alert that clears on recovery). Every capability shipped with MCP parity, guide/docs updates, and hot-upgrade-safe migrations, across six jj changes (afa4a89c..). 1448 tests green.
